policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'ye also have a Master in heaven' renders either the singular ouranoi or the plural ouranois; ASV uses 'in heaven' for both, and the three glossing notes here (Lords, bondservants, equality) touch other words. Nothing in the English distinguishes the number.
ASV 'that ye may know our state' has the second person plural verb, gnote, not the third singular gno ('that he may know').
ASV 'that ye may know our state' renders hemon; the RP hymon would give 'your state'.
ASV reads 'a servant of Christ Jesus', which renders the added Iesou; the short reading gives only 'of Christ'.
ASV 'that ye may stand perfect' renders either stathete or stete; both are aorist subjunctives of 'stand' and ASV's single verb does not distinguish them.
ASV 'and fully assured in all the will of God' renders peplerophoremenoi; peplaeromenoi would give 'filled'/'complete', not the assurance sense ASV states.
ASV 'that he hath much labor for you' renders polyn ponon; the RP zelon polyn would give 'much zeal'.

ASV 'Nymphas, and the church that is in their house' has the masculine accusative Nymphan (with the note 'The Greek may represent Nympha') and the plural auton; the textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read her' places autes in the margin, not in the ASV text, excluding the base and r01, while auton rather than autou is read.
Laodikeon and Laodikaion are orthographic variants of the same genitive plural; ASV 'the church of the Laodiceans' renders either, and the sole note (Greek the) concerns the article.
ASV ends 'Grace be with you.' with no 'Amen', so the RP addition of Amen is not rendered.
